title.narrative: Urban monitoring framework baseline data collection and validation for a Sample of Coastal Cities

description.narrative:
Quality, relevant, accessible, and timely urban data is a key element that supports the collective achievement of good governance, accountability and progress monitoring in cities across the world. Timely data and information help city authorities and decision makers to respond better to urban challenges and needs especially in periods where prioritization of scarce resources is needed. In addition, use of reliable, up to date, disaggregated, and accessible urban data ensures that decisions made by local and national governments, with the support from international agencies, civil society organizations, the private sector, and citizens at large, are evidence-based and leave no one or no space behind. Regular generation of accurate and reliable data also supports monitoring of progress against local development frameworks (e.g., city, regional and national development plans) and global agendas (e.g., 2030 Agenda/SDGs, New Urban Agenda, Paris Agreement, Sendai Framework, etc.). In addition to data, cities require a monitoring system that can help them collate, analyze and translate the data into simple to understand information and quick decision making. Such a system enables cities to track progress and identify setbacks to collective development and supports their formulation of evidence-based policies. In addition, cities also require periodic assessments on their state of development, and accurate tools to evaluate policy outcomes and the impact of specific plans and actions. Due to the high quality and quantities of data required for effective development monitoring, urban monitoring systems should be properly structured to allow for multi-level analysis and conversion of raw data into policy and decision-making processes. In partnership with countries and cities around the world, UN-Habitat through the Data and Analytics unit (DAU), (formerly Global Urban Observatory unit), has over the past two decades supported data collection for urban indicators (covering economic, environment, social, health, transport, and urban data), data analysis and regular dissemination of urban data. DAU further compiles, analyses, publishes urban indicator data, and maintains the Global Urban Indicator database. At the global level, UN-Habitat’s corporative approach on SDG/NUA localization is articulated around three main components: (i) Global Urban Monitoring Framework (UMF); (ii) Voluntary Local Review; (iii) SDG Cities Flagship Programme. Through this integrated approach, UN-Habitat is able to provide support throughout all stages of the SDG/NUA localization process: from data innovation to strategic planning, to policy formulation, monitoring and reporting.
The implementation of the UMF in Mombasa and Dar es salaam will directly contribute to the goal of the SDG cities flagship programme, which seeks to realize the potential of cities to drive the achievement of the SDGs by working with them (and other levels of government, communities, business sector and development partners) to connect the value chain of data; evidence-based policy; capacity in governance, planning and financing; and, impact investments, to accelerate the achievement of SDGs in cities. In addition, data produced from this project, and its compilation and analysis will directly contribute to UN-Habitat’s initiative on VLRs, through which the agency with partners undertakes research, provides guidance and supports cities to produce data informed VLRs. The rolling out of the UMF in the two cities will hence aim to collect the primary data for the producing the VLRs for the two cities and through this process we will facilitate more strategic work on SDG localization, and engagement in the SDG Cities project cycle particularly the qualification for the sample cities through the mechanisms of the SDG Cities Certification.
The Western Indian Ocean Marine Science Association (WIOMSA) has requested the Regional Office for Africa and the Data and Analytics Unit of UN-Habitat to support them in undertaking a UMF baseline data review and collection exercise in two cities in the west Indian ocean region that have substantial economic influence in their respective countries and the general blue economy. WIOMSA’s interest to undertake this project is informed by their interest in linking the knowledge that emerges from research to the management and governance issues that affect marine and coastal ecosystems in the region. Project Approach The project implementation strategy will entail data assessments and collection planning by reviewing the extent at which existing data can be used and its credibility to support the urban monitoring framework approach. In terms of indicators, the assessment will aim to draw on the UMF indicators framework including covering additional city-level aspects around inputs, outputs, outcomes, and impacts to reflect the key outcome of the project, which is to collect a baseline UMF indicators’ data.
